title: ChIP protocol

steps_raw.instruction: Supporting protocol on Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (Krishnaprasad et al., 2018)
Chromatin Immunoprecipitation

Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) experiment was performed as described in Panizza et al. 2011, Mendoza et al. 2009, and Thacker et al. 2014 with minor modifications, using native Msh5 antibody (From Prof. Akira Shinohara, Osaka University) and Protein A sepharose beads (GE Healthcare). The detailed protocol is as follows:
Yeast cell lysate preparation

50ml yeast culture was collected from the SPO medium (4 x107 cells/ml) and centrifuged at 4000 RPM for 5 minutes. The cell pellet was re-suspended in 1 ml lysis buffer and 900µl of glass beads was added (acid washed (425 -600 µm)). Cells were lysed by shaking in Mini-Beadbeater-8 (1 min x 18 times). The samples were kept on ice for 2 min between shaking. Breakage efficiency was measured by counting intact cell concentration before and after the cell breakage using hemocytometer.

After breakage, the top of the tubes were cleaned by wiping with 70% ethanol. A small hole was made at the top of the screw-cap tubes and placed inverted into a 15 ml polystyrene tube. Cell extract was collected by centrifugation (1 min, 4000 RPM, 4C). 1 ml lysis buffer was added to the beads and centrifuged again to completely collect cell lysate.

For sonication, 15 ml tube adaptor unit was inserted into the tubes. The metallic bar should not touch the wall of the tube. Bioruptor water tank was filled with pre-chilled Milli-Q water and one layer of ice. Cell extract was sonicated with low intensity 30 sec ON/ 30 sec OFF for 10 min (replenish ice after 10 min). Tank water was replaced with fresh pre-chilled Milli-Q water and one layer of ice; again sonicated for 10 min with the same setting. Water and ice were changed and sonication repeated with same settings once again. After the third round, lysate was transferred to 2 mL tube and centrifuged (13k RPM 5 min, 4C) to remove cell debris. The supernatant was transferred to a fresh 15 ml polystyrene tube. Ice and pre-chilled Milli-Q water was added to the water tank; lysate was sonicated for 10 min with the same setting. Water and ice were changed and repeated the sonication with same settings once again.
10 L lysate was collected for checking sonication efficiency. From each time point the samples were divided into two (at this stage samples can be stored at -80C)

To check for sonication efficiency, 190 L TE/1%SDS was added to 10 l lysate. DNA was extracted as mentioned in later section of this method. DNA was eluted with 30 L TE and half of the sample was run on 1.2 % agarose gel. An average fragment length of ~300 – 400bp should be obtained.

Protein A sepharose beads were prepared as per the manufacturer's protocol. 50 l protein A beads were used per sample. Beads were blocked by washing twice with 400 L PBS/BSA and incubating beads with 400 L PBS/BSA on rotating wheel at 4ºC for almost 4 h.

50 l protein A beads per sample was washed twice with 1 ml Lysis buffer. The lysate was kept for thawing on ice. To the washed beads lysate was added and kept for rotation at 4ºC for 1h (Pre-clearing).

Beads used for pre-clearing were separated by centrifugation at low speed (1000 RPM, 1 min) and the supernatant was collected. 10 l of the supernatant/lysate was collected for Western blotting and 20 l for Input sample, and kept at -20ºC and 4o, respectively. 5 l Msh5 antibody was added (2.5 l for each 1ml aliquot) to IP sample. Samples were kept for rotation at 4ºC for 6h. Blocked beads were washed twice with 400 L PBS/BSA. PBS/BSA was removed by centrifugation at low speed (1000 RPM, 1 min). Lysate and antibody mixture were added to the beads. Samples were kept at 4ºC for another 6h.

After the incubation of lysate with antibody and beads, centrifugation was performed at low speed (1000 RPM, 1 min), and 10l of lysate was collected from supernatant for Western blotting and kept at -20ºC. The rest of the lysate can be frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at -80ºC.

Beads were washed as mentioned below: two times with 1 ml lysis buffer, two times with 1 ml lysis buffer plus 360 mM NaCl, two times with 1 ml washing buffer, one time with 1 ml TE wash buffer. The sample was kept for rotation on a rotor for 3 min at room temperature upon each wash. During the first and the last wash, beads were suspended with washing solution and transferred to Protein LoBind tube.
The samples were centrifuged at low speed (1000 RPM, 1 min) to remove the supernatant completely.

For elution, 40 μL of elution buffer was added to the beads and incubated at 65ºC for 15 minutes with shaking. Centrifugation was performed at 13k RPM for 1 second and the supernatant was transferred into a new 1.5 mL tube. 160 L TE/1%SDS was added to the beads, vortexed and centrifuged at 13k RPM for 1 second, and the supernatant combined with the previous eluate. 10 l of eluate was collected for Western blotting (IP) and stored at -20ºC.
To the 20 L input sample collected earlier, 380 L of TE/1%SDS was added, then split into two aliquots.
1 L RNase A was added to all the samples and incubated overnight at 65ºC in a thermo block for removing RNA and to reverse the crosslinks.
To each of the 200 µL aliquots, 7.5 L of proteinase K (20 mg/mL) was added and incubated at 50ºC for 2 h in thermo block.

For DNA isolation 1 mL Buffer PB (QIAGEN) and 10 L of 3M Sodium acetate pH 5.2 was added and incubated at 37ºC for 30 minutes. DNA purification was done using column method with Qiagen PCR Purification Kit. The two WCE which was divided to two aliquots earlier were combined at this point, and the DNA was eluted with 50 µL TE pH 8.0. Samples were stored at -20ºC until analysis by sequencing or qPCR.

The eluted DNA was used for sequencing as well as qPCR. The sequencing was performed on Illumina platform from Fasteris, Switzerland. The DNA fragments were sequenced on Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform using a 50-bp single-end sequencing protocol. For qPCR two-step normalization was performed, first, the percentage enrichment from input was calculated followed by calculation of fold enrichment from the early 2h time point.
Lysis buffer: 50 mM Hepes-KOH pH 7.5, 140 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1% Triton X-100, 0.1% Na-deoxycholate.
PBS: 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 4.3 mM Na2HPO4, 1.47 mM KH2PO4, pH 7.4.
Washing buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 250 mM LiCl, 0.5% Na-deoxycholate, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5% Triton X-100.
TE wash buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5% Triton X-100.
Elution buffer: 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 10 mM EDTA, 1% SDS.
